The word sharp carries one powerful idea: the quality of cutting through something — cleanly, precisely, and intensely. A sharp knife cuts material. A sharp mind cuts through confusion. A sharp comment cuts through feelings. Once you understand this core idea, every meaning of the word will make sense.

Here is every meaning of sharp as an adjective, explained clearly.
1. Having a Fine Edge or Point (The Core, Literal Meaning)

This is the most basic sense of the word. A sharp object has an edge or point that is fine and precise enough to cut, pierce, or scratch things easily.

  • A sharp knife slices through food cleanly.
  • A sharp needle pierces fabric without effort.
  • A sharp pencil draws thin, precise lines.

The opposite of sharp in this sense is blunt or dull. A dull knife drags across food without cutting it properly.
2. Having a Clear, Well-Defined Edge or Outline

Something sharp can also mean its edges or boundaries are very clearly defined — crisp and distinct, not blurry or fuzzy.

  • A sharp photograph — every detail is crisp and clear, nothing is blurred.
  • A sharp contrast — one thing stands out very boldly against another; the difference is very clear.
  • A sharp jawline — a jaw with well-defined, clear edges (not soft or round).
  • A sharp turn on a road — the road bends at a steep, abrupt angle, not a gentle, gradual curve.
3. Sudden, Abrupt, and Intense

Sharp describes something that happens suddenly and all at once — like a quick, piercing stab.

  • A sharp pain — a sudden, intense pain that hits you in an instant, not a slow dull ache.
  • A sharp increase in prices — prices jumped up quickly and steeply.
  • A sharp drop in temperature — it became much colder very suddenly.
  • A sharp intake of breath — a sudden, quick breath you take when you are shocked or surprised.

The word captures both suddenness and intensity. A sharp change is not gradual — it happens fast and it is noticeable.
4. Intelligent, Quick-Thinking, and Perceptive

When used to describe a person or their mind, sharp means mentally quick, alert, and perceptive. Just as a sharp blade cuts through material easily, a sharp mind cuts through problems, confusion, and information easily.

  • She has a sharp mind — she understands things quickly, thinks clearly, and misses very little.
  • A sharp student — learns fast, catches things others might overlook.
  • Sharp eyes — notices details that others miss; very observant.
  • He is sharp as a tack (a common idiom) — he is extremely clever and quick-witted.

A sharp person does not need things explained twice. They pick things up fast and think on their feet.
5. Harsh, Cutting, and Severe (in Words, Tone, or Manner)

Just as a sharp knife can cut skin, sharp words can cut through feelings. When language, criticism, or someone's manner is described as sharp, it means it is blunt, harsh, and direct — possibly hurtful.

  • A sharp remark — a comment that is blunt and critical, possibly unkind.
  • Sharp criticism — feedback that is severe and hard-hitting, not soft or gentle.
  • She gave him a sharp look — a stern, piercing stare that expressed disapproval or warning.
  • A sharp tongue — a habit of saying things that are blunt, biting, or critical. Someone with a sharp tongue does not sugarcoat things.
  • A sharp reply — a quick, curt, and possibly cold response.

There is an important nuance here: being sharp is not always cruel. Sometimes it is simply very direct and honest — with no softening. But it can sting if the listener is not expecting it.
6. High-Pitched and Piercing (of Sounds)

A sharp sound cuts through the air and through the other noise around it. It is high, piercing, and sudden.

  • A sharp cry — a sudden, high-pitched cry, usually of pain or shock.
  • A sharp whistle — a piercing, high whistle that cuts through background noise.
  • A sharp crack — a sudden, loud, cutting sound, like a whip cracking or a branch snapping.

If you have ever heard a sound that made you flinch because it was so sudden and piercing, that is a sharp sound.
7. Strong and Pungent (of Taste or Smell)

A sharp taste or smell is strong, intense, and biting. It "hits" your senses suddenly and powerfully, almost the way a blade would.

  • Sharp cheese (like aged cheddar or blue cheese) — has a strong, intense, biting flavor that hits you immediately.
  • A sharp smell of vinegar — an intense, stinging smell.
  • A sharp taste — a flavor that is strong, biting, and often sour or tangy rather than mild or sweet.
8. Cold and Biting (of Weather)

Sharp weather is cold in a way that feels like it is cutting into you.

  • A sharp wind — a biting, cold wind that cuts right through your clothes.
  • A sharp frost — an intense, biting frost.
  • Sharp cold — a piercing, penetrating cold, not just mild chill.

You can almost feel the difference: "mild cold" is uncomfortable; "sharp cold" feels like the air is cutting into your skin.
9. Stylish and Well-Dressed (Informal)

This is a more informal, everyday usage, especially common in American English. When someone looks sharp or is described as sharp, they are very stylishly and impressively dressed.

  • He looked really sharp in his suit — he was dressed very well, stylish and put-together.
  • That is a sharp outfit — that is a very impressive, fashionable set of clothes.

This sense comes from the idea that someone who is sharp in appearance has a very "clean, crisp, well-defined" look — no sloppiness, everything in order.
10. Exactly (Used After a Time)

When placed after a time, sharp means "at that exact moment — not a minute before or after."

  • The meeting begins at 9 o'clock sharp — it begins exactly at 9:00.
  • Be here at noon sharp — be here at exactly noon, not 12:01 or 11:59.

This meaning comes from the idea of precision and exactness — just like the clean, precise cut of a sharp blade.
11. Steep and Abrupt (of Angles or Slopes)

A sharp angle or slope is steep and severe, not gradual or gentle.

  • A sharp angle — a narrow, tight angle (what is called an acute angle in geometry); two lines that meet at a tight, steep point.
  • A sharp slope — a slope that drops or rises steeply and suddenly.
  • A sharp bend in a road — a bend that turns at a steep angle, requiring you to slow down.
12. In Music

In music, sharp has a specific technical meaning. A sharp note is one that is played or sung half a step higher in pitch than its natural note. The symbol for this is ♯.

  • C♯ (C-sharp) is a note that is half a step higher than C.
  • F♯ (F-sharp) is half a step higher than F.

This connects to the broader idea: a sharp note is "raised up" — higher, more intense, more elevated in pitch.
Common Phrases and Expressions with Sharp

Understanding these phrases will help you recognize sharp in everyday use:

  • Keep a sharp eye / sharp lookout — watch very carefully and attentively; stay alert and observant.
  • Sharp as a tack / sharp as a whip — extremely clever, quick-witted, and mentally alert.
  • A sharp tongue — a tendency to speak bluntly, harshly, or critically.
  • Look sharp! — an instruction meaning hurry up! Move quickly!
  • Sharp practice — dishonest, cleverly deceptive, or borderline unethical behavior (especially in business).
  • In sharp contrast — the difference between two things is very clear, striking, and impossible to miss.
  • Sharp-eyed — very observant; quick to notice things.
  • Sharp-witted — mentally quick; clever and alert.
The One Idea That Connects Everything

Every single meaning of sharp comes back to this:

Something that cuts through — cleanly, precisely, and with intensity.

What is sharpWhat it cuts through
  • A sharp blade cuts through material.
  • A sharp mind cuts through confusion and complexity.
  • A sharp comment cuts through feelings.
  • A sharp pain cuts through your comfort.
  • A sharp image cuts through blurriness.
  • A sharp sound cuts through background noise.
  • A sharp wind cuts through warmth.
  • A sharp turn cuts abruptly across a path.

Whenever you meet the word sharp in something you are reading, ask yourself: what is "cutting through" something here? The answer will almost always reveal the meaning perfectly.
